uncertain.text: ſcrutables iugemẽs de la diuinité) plaiſans, ny agreables
uncertain.note: the mark printed between 'diuinité' and 'plaiſans' is not the fount's usual ')' (compare the bold right-bulging ')' of 'exemple)' two lines above). It prints as two thin segments leaning down to the right, from cap height to baseline, and reads like a worn or half-inked type. Sense requires the parenthesis opened at 'eſtre (s'il', so it is transcribed ')'. Alternative readings: a damaged '(' or a stray rule.

uncertain.text: Les mariages ainſi contractez auant l'aage legitime
uncertain.note: the final e of 'legitime' carries a heavy ink blot on its upper-right terminal that could be taken for an acute. It is attached to the letter, unlike the clearly detached acute of 'ordonné' on the next line, so it is read as plain e.

a small detached mark sits above the A of ARREST and another above the V of DV. Capitals carry no accents in this fount (§2), and both are far lighter than the type, so they are read as ink specks / offset and omitted. Letters are widely tracked (spaced capitals) but running_head has no spaced_caps field.

uncertain.text: Dieu: & moins la fin, pour laquelle ce ſainct & venerable
uncertain.note: a small dot sits at the baseline immediately after 'ſainct', about half the size of this fount's full stops and touching the t's terminal. Read as an ink speck or part of the ct ligature, not a full stop; sense ('ce ſainct & venerable eſtat') allows none.

uncertain.text: diſes & diſſolutions, auſquelles pluſieurs deſtituez de cõ
uncertain.note: 'pluſieurs' has an ink blob bridging the u and the long s, so the u could be misread as a or as u with a mark. Read as 'pluſieurs' from sense and letter shapes; no tilde is intended.
the tall letter in 'malefic.' has a crossbar on both sides of the stem in the italic fount, so it is f, not long ſ; the citation is the Decretals title 'de frigidis et maleficiatis'.

two small dots float above and to the right of the final e of 'minore', at different heights and sizes. They may be an ill-set or broken abbreviation mark (lex 'minorem', Dig. de ritu nuptiarum), but they are nothing like the flat tilde of 'canõ' in note b, so they are read as specks and the word is transcribed 'minore.'

uncertain.text: deſordonnées. Ie preuoy biẽ ici, qu'on m'oppoſera ie ne
uncertain.note: a small round dot floats at cap height in the space between 'm'oppoſera' and 'ie'. It is round, not the wedge-shaped apostrophe of 'm'oppoſera' just before it, and sits well above the line, so it is read as a speck / rising space and omitted.

the numeral is a plain serifed vertical with no dot, unlike the dotted i of 'Loy i.' in note d, so it is read as the arabic figure 1 (same shape as the folio 1 on p001). Note b's '1. & canõ qui' uses the same sort.
